findings.title: One zero-range bound (pin off / fuse cap at a DHW step) puts the whole solve on the scalar FD path: 9,222 steps/gradient
findings.claim: With one forced-off manual pin, or a power_caps_extra equal to the DHW run power (0.8 p_max) at the steps hot water is planned, the default two-zone DHW solve costs 9,222 simulate_step per gradient and 1.5-1.6 M steps (710-751x the reference solve) instead of 297 per gradient and 38x.
findings.mechanism: optimizer.py:_bounds_supported_by_batch returns False for any lo >= hi, so _multi_start_minimize passes jac=None and scipy estimates every gradient with n scalar objective calls (n scalar trajectories of n simulate_step each). solve_space produces the (0,0) bound whenever headroom = min(p_max - dhw, caps_extra - dhw) is 0; _apply_pins_to_bounds produces it for every forced-off pin. The golden fuse_guard fixture (cap 0.6 p_max) is already on this path: 731,904 simulate_step, 8.2 s. A cap at a single step was dodged by the plan (batched, 294/gradient), so the trigger is a DHW block coinciding with a capped step; a uniform fuse cap or a pin guarantees it. Pi 4 (x7 assumed): 2-3 min per solve every 30 min with the loop starved (D9-05).

findings.title: The stress gate cannot see a 2x or 4x solve regression: budgets 4.7x/8.9x above cost, no CI override, no memory line
findings.claim: Doubling HeatPumpOptimizer.optimize's work trips neither of tests/stress.py's relative checks: the worst scenario is 298.8x the reference against a 1400x budget and the sweep 50.7x against 450x, so the smallest uniform regression the gate can see is 4.69x.
findings.mechanism: SOLVE_BUDGET_RATIO=1400 and SWEEP_BUDGET_RATIO=450 were sized when the dearest scenarios cost 655-662x (tests/stress.py:165 still says so); the batched jac made every combination 10-20x cheaper and the budgets were not re-sized. .github/workflows/tests.yml and tests/run.sh set neither STRESS_SOLVE_RATIO nor STRESS_SWEEP_RATIO (grep 0), and tests/*.py contain no tracemalloc/getrusage/ru_maxrss (grep 0), so the gate sees only per-solve CPU above 4.7x and never memory.

findings.title: The batched jac re-evaluates f(x) scipy just computed: 2n scalar simulate_steps per gradient where n would do
findings.claim: On the batched path each gradient costs 96 batch rows plus 201 scalar simulate_step (two full scalar trajectories), because the jac closure recomputes objective(x) for its f0 right after scipy evaluated objective(x) at the same point; a one-entry memo halves the scalar steps per gradient to 101 and cuts solve CPU 13 %.
findings.mechanism: optimizer.py:_multi_start_minimize builds jac(x) = _batch_fd_gradient(batch_objective, a, x, float(objective(x, *a)), ...); scipy's ScalarFunction has just called objective(x) (nfev == njev == 103 in the two-zone DHW solve). The scalar simulation is 25 % of the solve's thread CPU, the batch 32 %.

findings.title: DHW planning costs 3.4-3.8x a reference solve and 63 % of a single-zone DHW solve; half is per-slot tank re-simulation
findings.claim: One _build_dhw_requirements call costs 64 simulate_dhw_only calls (6,144 Python-loop tank steps, 7,084 compute_cop_dhw calls) and 70-76 ms of M1 CPU, of which the min-run rounding is 43-59 %; two calls run per winter DHW solve, and in a single-zone winter DHW solve the planner is 63 % of the solve's CPU.
findings.mechanism: optimizer.py:_apply_dhw_min_run simulates the whole tank once per weak slot (trajectory(raised) per i in weak, plus a re-simulation after each zeroing); _plan_dhw_cheapest_first re-simulates per repaired violation (2-4 per pass, two passes); simulate_dhw_only is a Python loop with a compute_cop_dhw call per step. _co_optimize re-plans once more when space heating is pinned against the DHW headroom, doubling the planner cost.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: optimizer.py:_apply_dhw_min_run: raise all weak slots in one pass and simulate once, falling back to per-slot only when the joint trajectory breaches the ceiling (keeps the per-slot decision order on the fallback); thermal_model.py:simulate_dhw_only: hoist per-step attribute lookups. Order-preserving rewrites carry no golden drift; a joint-raise that changes which slots survive would drift DHW fixtures.
expected_golden_drift: none for an order-preserving rewrite; DHW fixtures if the joint-raise changes surviving slots

findings.title: The solve starves the event loop for its whole duration: 68-74 Hz loop vs 780 Hz idle, starvation share 0.97-0.998
findings.claim: With the solve in a ThreadPoolExecutor under a real asyncio loop, a 1 ms heartbeat wakes every 13-15 ms instead of every 1.3 ms for 96.7 % (batched two-zone DHW, 0.8 s) to 99.8 % (D9-01 path, 14.7 s) of the solve's wall time, with the longest contiguous hold 39-75 ms inside simulate_trajectory_batch.
findings.mechanism: The objective is Python plus small-array numpy, which holds the GIL between ops; the loop thread gets the GIL only through the 5 ms switch-interval hand-off, so every loop turn waits one hand-off plus the executor's current op. The two time.sleep(0.002) yields sit between L-BFGS-B starts and between the DHW and space stages (2 x 2 ms of an 800 ms solve), not inside an iteration. On a Pi 4 (x7 assumed) the same share persists for ~6 s per default solve and 2-3 min per D9-01 solve, every 30 minutes.
